body:
On 1998-06-22 jmc@Steam.Stanford.EDU said:
 jm>115. The system HAS TO force people to behave in ways that are
 jm>increasingly remote from the natural pattern of human behavior.
 jm>For example, the system needs scientists, mathematicians and
 jm>engineers. It can't function without them.
 jm>So heavy pressure is put on children to excel in these fields.
 jm>It isn't natural for an adolescent human being to spend the bulk of
 jm>his time sitting at a desk absorbed in study.
 jm>A normal adolescent wants to spend his time in active contact with
 jm>the real world.
 jm>Among primitive peoples the things that children are trained to do
 jm>tend to be in reasonable harmony with natural human impulses.
 jm>Among the American Indians, for example, boys were trained in
 jm>active outdoor pursuits - just the sort of things that boys like.
 jm>But in our society children are pushed into studying technical
 jm>subjects, which most do grudgingly.
 jm>Is it relevant that enormously more young people undertake to escape
 jm>from primitive societies to advanced societies than go the other
 jm>way? --

Most certainly, I say.
But somebody had to point out the downside from a new angle some day.
